newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI SHARES MUCH OVERVALUED - RAIFFEISEN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI SHARES MUCH OVERVALUED - RAIFFEISEN.

text.p: Shares in the largest Czech commercial bank Komercni Banka a.s. are heavily overvalued and would be more realistically priced at half the current rate, an analysis by Raiffeisen Bank says.

Shares in Komercni were trading at around 1,900 on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) on Friday, but citing poor earnings prospects and the need for massive new provisioning, the report said 900-1,000 crowns per share would be more appropriate.

"Under an optimistic scenario, assuming that 75 percent of the estimated collateral backing the bank's loss loans can be collected...we would value the bank at book value or CZK 1,450 per share," the report said.
"A more realistic scenario which assumes that only 50 percent of the collateral can be collected, values the bank at approximately CZK 900-1,000 per share."
Komercni was not available for immediate comment.
The most immediate cause of concern to Raiffeisen was the alleged need for more than 40 billion crowns in provisions.

"Komercni Banka is significantly under-provisioned. We estimate that at least CZK 8.5 billion in provisions are needed immediately, and that another 32 billion would be necessary if the bank were to provision by U.S. standards."
The report added that profitability would be threatened by declining net interest margins, forecast to fall to 3.4 percent by the end of this year and 3.2 percent in 1998.

It also said that competition would increase with the sale of Agrobanka and a 36 percent stake in IPB Bank to foreign buyers and that comsumer loans accounted for only five percent of Komercni's loan book making it overly exposed to the business cycle.

The report also rejected the notion that Komercni, the most heavily weighted Czech banking stock accounting for 11 percent of the official PX50 index's capitalisation, should be held as a proxy for the Czech market.
"There are other issues on the Prague exchange (e.g. SPT Telecom) which also act as proxies and contain far less downside risk."
